name: loxilb
what_it_is: loxilb is an open-source, eBPF-based cloud-native load-balancer written in Go, targeting Kubernetes service type LoadBalancer for on-prem, public-cloud, and hybrid environments. It is purpose-built for telco/5G workloads that require exotic protocols such as GTP, SCTP multi-homing, PFCP, NGAP, SRv6, and SEPP.
components: loxilb-ingress Kubernetes Ingress controller (separate repo: loxilb-io/loxilb-ingress)
REST API server (port 11111 default, TLS port 8091)
measurement: Extensive end-point liveness probes (active and passive --passive-probe)
configuration: --cloud : cloud type e.g. aws, ncloud (default on-prem)
--cloudcidrblock : VIP CIDR block for cloud deployments
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection mechanism found in the repository
HA clustering with BFD-based hitless failover (--ka flag) can be used to simulate node failure scenarios
Passive liveness probes (--passive-probe) detect endpoint failures without active health checks
modes: BGP peer-only mode (-r / --peer, goBGP only, no datapath)
constraints: Requires privileged container (privileged: true) and root user to load eBPF programs and manage network interfaces
Host kernel must support eBPF; tested on Ubuntu 20.04, 22.04, 24.04, and RedHat 9
macvlan or bridge networks required for production multi-node deployments (as seen in docker-compose); pure overlay-only environments may need additional configuration
eBPF sockmap L7 acceleration (--sockmapsupport) and several other options are marked experimental and may not be stable
Multi-cluster support is planned but not yet released (marked 🚧 in README)
Kubernetes Network Policy support is not yet implemented (unchecked in README feature list)
docker_services: loxilb (image: ghcr.io/loxilb-io/loxilb:latest, privileged, root, networks: bridge + macvlan)
notable_absences: No docker-compose file at repository root; compose files are only in cicd/ test subdirectories
No built-in fault injection or chaos tooling
No multi-cluster support (planned, not yet available)
No Windows support (Linux eBPF kernel dependency)
